I’m helping my father choose between the generic oral antihistamines cetirizine and loratadine for seasonal allergy symptoms. I eventually need a plain-language handout at `allergy-options.md`, tailored to his situation. I’ll give you his health and day-to-day-use details in my next message and tell you when to do the research and draft the handout.

When I ask you to proceed, use live web research from current, reachable U.S. government health sources. Compare only cetirizine and loratadine; do not name brands or introduce any third allergy medicine. The final handout must be 500–850 words and use exactly these headings, in this order, with no other headings: `## Bottom line`, `## Side-by-side`, `## Safety for this situation`, `## When to get help`, and `## Sources`. Put a Markdown comparison table in `Side-by-side`. Give a clear starting choice for someone who needs to drive during the day, explain why, and plainly state the important uncertainty rather than claiming one drug is universally better. Retain every health and symptom detail I give you. Include practical label-use and drowsiness guidance, routine and emergency help guidance, and exactly four distinct Markdown links to sources you actually consulted. All four links must use HTTPS, be from U.S. government `.gov` sites, appear in `Sources`, and include an access date. Deliver the completed handout itself, not a plan or a description of what you would write.
